is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles gambiae s.l. (page 1, abstract).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper reports genotyping for kdr (L1014F/S) and Ace-1 (G119S) mutations (page 3, 'Knock-down resistance (kdr) and Ace-1 genotyping').

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: The paper reports the allelic frequency (0.98) for kdr-e (page 4, 'Knock-down (kdr) and Ace-1 genotyping').

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected in the field in Muleba, Tanzania (page 3, 'Study area').

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an empirical study reporting original field data and bioassays.

sub_country_location.evidence: The study was conducted in Kyamyorwa and Kiteme villages, Muleba District, Tanzania (page 3, 'Study area').

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The study covers collections in 2011 and 2012 (page 3, 'Mosquito sampling').

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study is part of a larger cluster randomized trial (West et al., 2014), but this paper reports specific insecticide resistance monitoring data not presented in the main trial paper.

supplement.evidence: All necessary data is provided in the main text and tables.

assessment.summary: This study monitored insecticide resistance in Anopheles gambiae s.l. in two villages in Muleba, Tanzania, during a cluster randomized trial of LLINs and bendiocarb-based IRS. It reports high phenotypic resistance to pyrethroids and DDT, and a significant decrease in susceptibility to bendiocarb in the IRS-sprayed village. Genotyping confirmed high frequency of kdr mutations, while no Ace-1 (G119S) mutation was detected.
